notes.title: GOOD NEWS !
notes.notes:
[u][b]Hello everyone,[/b][/u]

Today, I can confirm that Infection Crisis is back in development.
The issues like animations, engine changes, and similar problems have been resolved.

You can check out the progress on animations on the YouTube channel, where there will be plenty of development videos about Infection Crisis.

As promised, I’m continuing to work on everything. I’m still working on the entire project alone, so things will move slower.
But the important thing is that updates will come, and the game will shine in a new light.

When the update arrives, if I feel it aligns with my original vision, the game will leave Early Access.
Unfortunately, Co-op will probably be removed — but it might be added later. I don’t want to confirm anything, so I’ll say: maybe Co-op will come later.

Thank you to everyone who stuck around during this tough period for Infection Crisis, and of course, to those who bought the game.
I’m continuing to work on it — follow the Discord and YouTube channel for more updates about development.

[b]Best regards![/b]

notes.title: Bad news....
notes.notes:
[u][b]Hello everyone,[/b][/u]

I want to reach out to all of you who have purchased or supported Infection Crisis. I need to inform you that the game is facing serious issues, and development may most likely not continue.

[b]Main Issues[/b]
The biggest challenge has been animations for weapons, items, and all other holdable objects. Each weapon was supposed to have its own unique animation, and I managed to achieve great results. However, the engine required something different, and for reasons I still don’t fully understand, everything moves up to the wrist, but the hands do not respond to animations. If all customization options for the weapon are disabled, the animations work, but then nothing functions properly—everything breaks, animations glitch, and sometimes the engine even crashes.

Additionally, Unreal Engine has been quite buggy, constantly breaking structures and causing issues with game packaging. When this happens, the entire game needs to be rebuilt from scratch. It’s not that I don’t want or don't love working on the game again, but after nine complete rebuilds of Infection Crisis, I simply don’t have the strength to start over once more.

The animation issues have completely drained me. An insane amount of time has been invested, only for everything to fall apart due to a single engine crash... Despite the struggle, working on this game for the past three and a half years has been an incredible experience that I will never forget. So many great people have followed my work, and I want to thank each and every one of you. Your support has been my greatest motivation during difficult times.

I hope you understand—I simply don’t want to release a half-finished product or something that only resembles a proper game. Of course, my game was never going to be at the level of a full team of professionals, but I also refuse to release something pretending to be good when it’s actually terrible.

[i][u][b]What’s Next?[/b][/u][/i]
This is not a final farewell or an official end to development. I just need to take a break, gather my thoughts, and try to fix the animations that must be in the game. Only then can we talk about continuing development. Writing this is incredibly difficult for me because a huge part of my dream is falling apart—but at the same time, part of it has already come true.

I hope no one is upset. I will do my best to fix the animations and complete the game as it deserves to be. I don’t want to blame my friends or anything that has happened over these past three and a half years—the only one responsible is me, whether due to my lack of knowledge or my knowledge itself. Infection Crisis was supposed to be a beautiful chapter in my life, and though it didn’t turn out exactly as planned, it still means a lot to me.

For now, I’ve gained a lot of experience, and let this serve as a promise to those who bought the game and believed in me: Infection Crisis will receive a new update that will change the game entirely. When will that be? I honestly don’t know. I would love for it to happen in a month, but it could take a year or more...

Planned Features for the Next Update :
[list]
[*] A new inventory system
[*] A new UI
[*] A new AI system
[*] Wild and domestic animals
[*] New house and building interiors
[*] New buildings and cities
[*] Three new maps, each with unique functions
[*] A campaign (story mode)
[*] New weapons
[*] A new character (FPP only, with fully interactive items)
[*] New gameplay mechanics
[*] Seasons and weather effects (rain, snow, drought, etc.)
[*] Traders
[*] A new building system
[*] Farms (Plants, berries, fruits and vegetables)
[*] And much more...
[/list]

Everything is possible to create, but when an animation that should work—one with absolutely no technical issues—simply refuses to function, even after 10, 15, or 20 hours of troubleshooting, it becomes a serious problem...

Stay healthy, take care of your families, and stay positive!
Best regards,
Brane, 
aka Branko, aka BJS Studio.

notes.title: Important Announcement for the Upcoming Update
notes.notes:
[b]Hello everyone,[/b]

I wanted to reach out and let you know that we are still hard at work on the new update. The game isn't dead, haha. To be honest, it never really took off, but we're still working on it. Some of the new features coming with the update will be almost as significant as when Apple releases a new iOS update. But that's not important right now.
What I want to talk about today is that the new update will bring a completely redesigned world, so you'll be able to enjoy new landscapes and a much richer map. I'm planning maps that are 4x4 km in size, featuring massive mountains, each with its own unique features. But that's a topic for another day, as the initial budget for something like that is around €800, which is currently out of reach for me. But we're making do with what we have, haha.


The next big change with the update is the complete removal of the third-person view. The game will now be entirely first-person. Why is that, and will it ever return in the future? The primary reason is that first-person animations are much easier to create—you only work with two hands. In contrast, with third-person, you have to coordinate the entire body with the first-person perspective, weapons, items, and so on.

Under all possible conditions, you'll be able to hold EVERY item in the game in your hands. Of course, this is also a massive undertaking because we currently have 194 items in the game, and the plan is to have around 250-300. The game is going to be quite complex, but that's the goal. There will be an online guide and an in-game tutorial to help you out.

Why am I planning to make it so complicated? Simply because I want this game to stand out from EVERY other survival game out there. Most survival games are relatively easy; survival is just about not dying from hunger, thirst, and AI.

The AI will also be getting improvements, with new zombie sounds. They will only spot you up close but will react to noise, so you'll have to be careful about how you use your weapons.

The images you see are still WORKS IN PROGRESS, so everything is subject to change.

Additionally, there will be new player animations, weapon animations, and more. All of this takes a lot of time, so the current version of Infection Crisis will remain as it is until the new update shines in its full glory.

Multiplayer is also something that we will be working on a lot because survival games are much more fun with two, three, or more players.

In conclusion, please be patient. I’m not sure when the update will be released, but once it’s out, it’s going to be something special. The next stop is realism in terms of everything—animations, maps, zombies, etc. I sincerely hope that this update will be released before 01.10.2024, as the game needs to be ready for Halloween, a holiday celebrated worldwide (except in Serbia, haha), but we’ll be sure to honor it!

Additionally, new languages will soon be available, such as Chinese, Brazilian Portuguese, German, and other similar languages.

Thank you for taking the time to read this. I would also like to ask you to join our Discord, where I’ll be posting new short updates and more. The more of us there are on Discord, the better, as we can communicate without any issues. :)

notes.title: Announcement for the new big update for Infection Crisis.
notes.notes:
Hello everyone!

Today, I want to address you after a long time. As you know, one of the major updates of this year has been announced. Unfortunately, agriculture will come a bit later. If there are any changes, you will be informed.

Since I've finished everything related to characters, and everything is as it should be in the mechanical world of the game for now, I've started working on the map. I want to beautify it and make it look the way it should.

The map is a very complex part of the game, but of course, I manage to put some things together. I want players to truly feel the pleasure of the game when they literally walk around the map and explore the surroundings.

Many things have been changed, so we will go through each item individually with screenshots directly from the engine. The map is only 20% complete, for the simple reason that details are crucial on the map. Of course, everything you see is subject to change, in terms of adding more details and surrounding elements.

[h2][u][b]Forests[/b][/u][/h2]
One of the biggest changes has been made to the forests. Let's start with the new trees, which aren't the best thing that could have happened, but for now, they're okay. They look very nice during gameplay, and they will look even better once everything is set in place.
Regarding the placement of trees and their positioning on the map, each tree will be MANUALLY placed on the map.
I also want to mention that there may be, but not necessarily, new mechanics for tree cutting. However, this is all in the development stages and everything is uncertain.

In the forests, you can find areas with berries, bushes, and probably some other plants that you can collect in the forests. I want to create mushrooms that you can eat. Of course, there will be poisonous ones as well as edible ones.

The grass and vegetation have been altered, especially designed for forests, as the grass in the forest and on the meadow are not the same as in real life. Fallen branches and similar things have been added.

[img]https://i.ibb.co/xDwCVgb/Screenshot-2.png[/img]

[h2][u][b]Rivers and Lakes[/b][/u][/h2]

Rivers and lakes have also undergone the biggest update. Sea grass, algae, sea stones, and more have been added.
I'm trying to add a fish world as well, but even if they are added, they won't be catchable. Until sometime in the future when those fish become catchable.

Of course, everything is still in the development stage, so everything will be more abundant and numerous.

[img]https://i.ibb.co/47qMVdH/Screenshot-1.png[/img]



[h2][u][b]Great Lake[/b][/u][/h2]

The largest lake has also undergone a significant visual update.
The beach has been completely redesigned and tidied up. Decorative palm trees, new textures, etc., have been added.
As I mentioned, many things will be added in the realization of the update.

[img]https://i.ibb.co/8Mt6RjQ/Screenshot-3.png[/img]

[h2][u][b]Rivers (outer part)[/b][/u][/h2]

Rivers have received gravel on the sides to make them look more realistic. Perhaps there will be further improvements. :)

[img]https://i.ibb.co/zN0LLpq/Screenshot-4.png[/img]



I hope you like how everything is shaping up. Of course, there's still a lot to be done. In addition to my daytime job, I have plenty to do with the game. I'm working bit by bit, taking it slow, and I want the story for the map to come to a close and, as we say in my country, to "put the dot on the i," ensuring everything is as it should be.

I haven't mentioned it above, but the weather will look different; everything will be synchronized and sorted out. So, there won't be fog during clear skies or maximum visibility during heavy rain or storms. And soon, as we approach the game's first release, it's not out of the question that seasons, a clock, days, and months of the year will be introduced. Realistic snow, rain, etc., are also on the horizon.

There are big plans, high expectations, a small budget, but strong ambitions. I'll say it again: I won't give up on the game. The only possibility of giving up would be when my computer becomes too weak for its development. It's not really giving up, more like taking a long break.

Unfortunately, we're reaching the point where 32GB of RAM is becoming insufficient, and even the Ryzen 5 3600x is becoming too weak for this kind of usage, but it's holding up.

Be patient. I hope this update will be released by the end of May, if not by mid-June. Stay healthy, love your loved ones, and be happy. The new update is coming :)

Warm regards,
BJS Studio.

notes.title: Infection Crisis - Current game situation
notes.notes:
[h1]Greetings everyone,[/h1]

The main and only developer of the Infection Crisis game is addressing you. Infection Crisis has encountered a significant problem in which all structures have been disrupted. The save game function has stopped working, all buildings had an error that was not visible but was present.
Unfortunately, everything related to items, buildings, and game mechanics must be rebuilt from scratch. I am not sad; Infection Crisis will gain a new life. I am happy to be able to redo everything from scratch. Fortunately, I have backups for the inventory, widgets, animations (default but... 😀 ) and similar things. So, the bunker is saved; now we just need to create some accompanying stuff.
Unfortunately, I do not want to guarantee, but I sincerely hope that the STABLE UPDATE will come by 15-25.02.2024.

I apologize to everyone for such an update, but unfortunately, the Unreal Engine itself is quite buggy; something works today, and tomorrow it doesn't. So, what I want to tell you is that no one has ever stopped the wind in this world, so no Unreal Engine will stop BJS Studio from working on Infection Crisis. The motivation is high, so now I have a strong obligation to the entire community, even though there are only a few people like:
[h2]Ecaps, Koko, Old Raver Gamez, Henrique.[/h2]

I want to express my greatest thanks to you, as you are currently the reason why I won't give up on the game. Of course, giving up is not an option; giving up is just a blueprint so bugged that even Epic Games themselves couldn't fix it, hahaha. A little humor doesn't hurt 🙂
See you soon, follow the website, Discord, and Steam Community.
Stay alive and healthy!


Branko / BJS Studio

Welcome to Infection Crisis: Fight For Life.
I wish you a lot of fun, exploration, and maybe a bit of frustration from dying, hahaha.

---

Dobrodosli u Infection Crisis Fight For Life.
Zelim vam puno zabave, istrazivanja i mozda malo nerviranja zbog umiranja hahaha.
